I farm 36 mu, and with some people in my household working off-farm, I will keep this year practical and not too labor-heavy. I have grown these crops for a long time, so I will stay with the crops I know: maize for steady grain, cotton for cash income, and mungbean on a smaller area because it needs less fertilizer and helps spread risk. Since I have well irrigation, I will use it to protect yield, but I will still avoid putting too much land into the most labor-demanding crop. I will put the largest area into summer maize because it is the most reliable for me under my conditions. I will keep cotton on a moderate area because it can bring cash but needs more management and picking labor. I will keep mungbean on a smaller area because it fits my labor situation and gives me another source of income if weather or price goes against one crop. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it matters for stable yield, use moderate fertilizer rather than very high rates, irrigate according to crop need, and use rotary tillage because it is faster and suits my scale.
